what: EPAM builds software for other companies. Its engineers, originally mostly in Eastern Europe and now spread across India and Latin America, design and write applications for large enterprises.
customers: Large companies in financial services, life sciences, travel, media and retail outsourcing software development.
moat: A reputation for engineering quality at the top of the outsourcing market, which lets it charge more per hour than Indian competitors on the same kind of work.
risks: The war in Ukraine forced it to move thousands of engineers, and the cost base is still being rebalanced
AI coding tools may reduce the hours companies need to buy
Revenue was flat at $4.7B for two years before recovering
opportunities: 18.8 times earnings and 16.3 times free cash flow with $470M of free cash flow
Revenue grew to $5.5B last year, and analysts see about 15% upside
watch: Organic revenue growth and utilisation of the engineering workforce.
